title: Provisional-bucket settlement worker for out-of-order token ingestion
creator: Elena Morris
summary: Introduce a buffer-and-settlement worker that holds provisional token counts for late-arriving events and produces idempotent final settlements to downstream billing.
description: Problem: Our current ingestion pipeline applies token usage to customer ledgers immediately on first-arrival. Out-of-order events (edge retries, regional ingestion lag, or replayed sessions) cause over-counting or multiple settlement steps when downstream reconciliations run, creating noisy retroactive credits and billing churn. Goal: Add a provisional-bucket worker that holds incoming token deltas for a configurable window (per-tenant, per-route), emits provisional metrics to the analytics pipeline, and then atomically reconciles and produces a single final settlement record when the window closes or when idempotent flush conditions are met. The worker must: 1) be horizontally scalable, 2) guarantee idempotency for repeat deliveries, 3) support tenant-level overrides for window length and risk profile, 4) expose observability for provisional vs final settled volume, and 5) integrate with existing rollback and playbook flows.
acceptance_criteria: Provisional-bucket worker deployed behind feature flag and configurable per-tenant
Late-arrival events within configured window are aggregated to a provisional bucket rather than immediate final ledger writes
Final settlement emits a single idempotent settlement message containing delta vs provisional and a settlement_id
Downstream billing joiner accepts provisional metrics for near-real-time dashboards and replaces them with final settlement upon closure
End-to-end test simulating out-of-order deliveries shows no double-count in final ledger and <0.5% false-positive credits
Monitoring dashboards show provisional volume, settlement latency distribution, and a reconciliation error rate metric
high_level_design_notes: Use a sharded provisional-store keyed by (tenant_id, route, window_start) implemented with DynamoDB/Bigtable for strong per-key writes and TTL-based expiry
Worker will accept events from existing ingestion Kafka topic, apply an idempotency key derived from request_id + seq when present
Emit provisional metrics to analytics with tag provisional=true and settlement_id=null. On closure emit final settlement with settlement_id and provisional=false
Settlement messages contain: tenant_id, route, window_start, settlement_id, final_token_delta, provisional_token_total, source_watermark
Rollout via feature flag with traffic mirroring to compare existing final-ledger path vs provisional path for accuracy before full cutover
implementation_plan: Prototype provisional-store schema and single-worker reconciliation loop (2 days)
Add idempotency helper library and deterministic settlement_id generation (1 day)
Integrate worker with ingestion consumer, emit provisional metrics to analytics topic (3 days)
Build final settlement writer with transactional write to final ledger topic and tombstone of provisional bucket (2 days)
Add observability (Prometheus metrics, console dashboards, alerting) and end-to-end test harness (3 days)
Gradual rollout: mirror -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with canary reconciliation checks (ongoing)
test_plan: Unit tests for idempotency and settlement_id determinism
Property tests simulating reordered batches and duplicates
Integration tests with analytics consumer to validate provisional->final transitions
Chaos test: delayed regional replicator to validate late-arrival behavior
Performance: sustain target throughput of 5k events/s per shard with p95 processing latency <200ms
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: >1% of settlements failing reconciliation in 10m window
Dashboard: provisional vs final volume, top tenants by provisional churn, settlement latency heatmap
migration_and_rollout: Start with low-risk tenants (internal + 3 small customers) behind feature flag
Run in mirror mode for 48h comparing existing ledger writes vs provisional+settlement; generate diff report
If diffs <0.1% for 48h increase traffic incrementally and keep automated rollback on diff spike
After 2 weeks of stable operation, enable default 15m windows for all new tenants and provide opt-out for legacy tenants
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: provisional buckets accumulate due to stuck workers -> Mitigation: TTL and escalation alert + auto-repairer job
Risk: idempotency key collisions under high cardinality -> Mitigation: include route and event fingerprint, verify against replay test harness
Risk: downstream systems mis-consume provisional metrics -> Mitigation: clearly tagged provisional metrics and consumer contract update with versioning
Risk: longer settlement windows increase latency to final billing -> Mitigation: per-tenant configurable window and SLOs documented
